GitHub code search (as opposed to repository-name search) requires authentication and was not run.

statusReasoning: PRELIMINARY_CLEARANCE_NO_HIGH_CONFLICT_FOUND requires real evidence from at least one official trademark registry AND thorough public-source searching with no same-category conflict. Only the second condition is met — zero of six target registers (TMview, EUIPO, INPI, WIPO, USPTO, UKIPO) was reachable, so that status is unavailable. CONFLICT_HIGH is also wrong: nothing found is a same-category conflict. Between INCONCLUSIVE_TOOL_LIMITATION and REVIEW_REQUIRED, REVIEW_REQUIRED was chosen because it is the strictly larger statement: it covers the registry blackout AND the substantive unresolved signal that no tool limitation explains away — a third party registered and parked coretend.com four months ago and this screening cannot determine who or why.
limitations: TMview not queryable — POST-only API, ECONNRESET on GET.
EUIPO eSearch plus not queryable — JavaScript SPA, no server-rendered results.
WIPO Global Brand Database not queryable — CAPTCHA gate before any data.
USPTO TMsearch not queryable — JavaScript SPA, empty shell returned.
UKIPO not queryable — primary host unresolvable, alternate host HTTP 403.
Secondary trademark mirrors (Justia Trademarks, Trademarkia, uspto.report) all HTTP 403.
RDAP for .app and .io unreachable; their availability rests on DNS delegation evidence only.
No similarity or phonetic trademark search was possible — only exact and hand-listed variant strings were checked.
No unregistered / common-law rights search (business registers, trade directories, social handles, EU/FR company names).
Apple App Store queries covered the US storefront only.
GitHub code search, private repositories, and pending/unpublished trademark applications are structurally invisible to this method.
Web-index evidence reflects only what is crawled and indexed; a recently launched or recently filed name may not appear.
No non-Latin-script, transliteration, or Cyrillic/CJK variant screening was performed.
authorises: Publishing the free, open-source, unsigned pre-release/beta as github.com/ahmetbsbnr/coretend with a site at coretend.ahmetbsbnr.com, using 'CoreTend' as a plain product name.
Using the name with NO registration symbol and NO claim, statement or implication of registration, clearance or legal validation anywhere (README, site, release notes, app UI, About panel).
Linking to Documentation/CORETEND_TRADEMARK_SCREENING.md as the honest record of what was and was not checked.
doesNotAuthorise: Any commercial use of the name — paid version, paid tier, brand-tied donations, App Store distribution, sponsorship, or any monetisation.
Use of the ® symbol, any claim of registration, or any wording implying trademark clearance, legal validation or attorney review.
Filing a trademark application on the strength of this document.
Building brand equity that would be expensive to unwind — trademark licensing, printed material, paid marketing, a logo lockup treated as final, or acquiring further domains.
Flipping legalReviewStatus to 'accepted' or publicReleaseAllowed to true; REVIEW_REQUIRED is not the 'accepted' that Scripts/check-brand-clearance.sh --publication waits for.

Treating 'no conflict found' as 'no conflict exists' — a registered CoreTend mark in class 9 or 42 in the EU, France, the UK, the US or under Madrid may exist and would not have been visible to any tool used here.
recommendedHumanStep: Commission a paid professional trademark search from a trademark attorney or professional search provider, covering Nice classes 9 and 42 across EUIPO, INPI (FR), UKIPO, USPTO and WIPO/Madrid, including similarity and phonetic searching — that is the step that can produce a real clearance opinion, which this document cannot. In parallel: (a) identify the registrant behind coretend.com via registrar WHOIS or a watch service, without contacting them before taking advice; (b) set a watch on CoreTend/Coretend in classes 9 and 42 and on the .com/.app/.io domain set; (c) optionally re-run this automated screening from an environment with browser automation, which could query the JavaScript register front-ends and convert several limitations into evidence.
